description: The settings every repository shares. A version is proposed only once it has been public for two days, so that a release pulled or fixed in its first days never reaches a branch; seven days held back the releases of anything published more often than once a week. internalChecksFilter is already strict by default; it is stated so that the wait is read here as holding back the branch and the pull request themselves, not only a status check on them. platformAutomerge is off so that whatever a repository lets Renovate merge waits for the pull request's checks as Renovate sees them, without relying on the repository's auto-merge setting or branch protection. Updates are proposed once a week, on Sunday in Tokyo, because a branch for every release of every dependency every day was more pull requests than anyone could read. The window is the whole day for two reasons: the repositories release whatever Renovate has merged as a patch version on Monday at 09:00 in Tokyo, so what opens on Sunday can be merged in time for that release, where a pull request opened on Monday would wait a week; and a self-hosted Renovate that runs once a day still meets a window of a whole day, where it would miss one of a few hours. The schedule only holds back new branches. A pull request already open is still rebased and moved to a newer release during the week, and what a repository lets Renovate merge is still merged, since updateNotScheduled and automergeSchedule are left as they are. A fix for a known vulnerability does not wait for Sunday: Renovate ignores the schedule, and the two-day wait, for vulnerabilityAlerts. Those come from the repository's Dependabot alerts, which have to be turned on; osvVulnerabilityAlerts adds the same kind of fix from the OSV database, which Renovate downloads whole and queries on its own machine. It needs nothing from the repository's settings, so it works the same for the Renovate app and for a self-hosted Renovate, and for private repositories, whose dependencies are never sent anywhere. OSV covers the packages of languages (npm, PyPI, Go modules, RubyGems, crates, Maven, NuGet, Packagist, Hex and Hackage), and only the dependencies named directly; it has nothing for Docker images, Kustomize or GitHub Actions, so a repository that has only those gets nothing from it

logLevelRemap.description: A repository that sets minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour to timestamp-optional for some dependencies has asked for them to go ahead without a release time, yet Renovate still warns each time it does so, and the warning lands among the Dependency Dashboard's repository problems. Reported as info, the expected behaviour no longer hides the real problems. Only these two messages are matched, so every other warning stays a warning
logLevelRemap.matchMessage: /^Some (release|upgrade)\(s\) did not have a releaseTimestamp, but as we're running with minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour=timestamp-optional, proceeding/

packageRules.description: The official ubuntu image is proposed without the two-day wait. Docker Hub gives a tag's last push as its release time, and the official ubuntu tags are pushed again every day or two, so a tag seldom looks two days old and an update would hardly ever be proposed. The rule is here for every repository, whether it uses the image today or not, so that a base changed to ubuntu later does not fall into the same trap. The name is matched as it is written, not as Docker Hub resolves it, so each way of writing the image is listed. The pull request's checks still have to pass

Workflows are already read by the github-actions manager. Grouping them keeps a handful of actions from arriving as a handful of pull requests, since they are updated together and reviewed the same way. Everything the manager reads is in the group, runners and the versions given to setup actions included. A repository that wants one of them on a branch of its own, such as a Node kept in step with its image, gives it another groupName in its own packageRules, which come after these
